chunks: Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Abdullah ibn Jundub, from Hisham ibn Salim, who said:
Hafs al-Aʿwar asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام while I was present, and he said:

My father had a hired worker, and that worker had something with him. Then the worker died, leaving behind neither an heir nor any relatives, and I have become distressed over that; what should I do? He said: “The needy are your concern; the needy are your concern.”
So I said: “May I be your ransom, I have indeed been troubled by that; what should I do?” He said: “It is like the way of your own wealth; if a claimant comes, you should give it to him.”
ai.seo_question: What should be done with the property of a deceased person who leaves no known heirs or relatives?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling concerning property left behind by a deceased hired worker who has no known heir or relative. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام directs attention to the needy, while also instructing that the property be held and treated like one's own wealth in the meantime, with the obligation to hand it over if a rightful claimant later appears.
